IEE Colloquium on Signal Processing for ESM Systems
abstract: An extremely efficient and flexible algorithm is presented. Two-pass multidimensional clustering provides optimal sorting of stable and agile radars. The use of pulse density allows control over size and position, and tolerance to measurement errors. The efficiency allows a simple, low cost implementation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Introduction to optical transform image modulation techniques and their application to ESM data processing
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Signal Processing for ESM Systems
abstract: Processing methods employing optical transform image modulation techniques (OTIM), have shown that very significant improvements in signal-to-background discrimination and clutter rejection can be achieved for remote sensing applications, and current research shows that these methods can also be incorporated into electro-optic data processing schemes with significant advantages. The capability of OTIM configurations to manipulate signals in several domains simultaneously also brings additional benefits.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The application of pattern recognition techniques to ESM data processing
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Signal Processing for ESM Systems
abstract: The application of pattern recognition techniques to ESM data processing has been studied, with particular reference to pulse-by-pulse analysis using intra-pulse parameters alone. Many current pulse deinterleaving methods are based on batch processing using time-of-arrival-difference (TOAD) analysis, which is both computationally expensive (especially in highly dense environments) and unreliable in certain scenarios (for example in the presence of agile emitters). The use of pattern recognition techniques has been suggested as an alternative approach to the deinterleaving of pulse data which would allow continuous (rather than batch) analysis on a pulse-by-pulse basis based on intra-pulse parameters alone (replacing TOAD analysis). This paper presents the conclusions of this study, and makes some recommendations for future work.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Signal processing for the ground based 'BLAST' ESM/ECM system
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Signal Processing for ESM Systems
abstract: Describes some data processing routines of the 'BLAST' ESM/ECM system developed by AEG. Furthermore, envisaged system upgrades are discussed. Finally, some field test results and their impact on the development of the 'PASSAT' ESM System are outlined. 'PASSAT' is a purely passive derivative of the 'BLAST' system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: SADIE-a high performance ESM signal analysis processor
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Signal Processing for ESM Systems
abstract: ESM systems have shown an insatiable appetite for processing power to handle ever denser and more complex radar pulse environments. In response to this, Racal Defence has developed a new ESM signal processor called SADIE which uses a new architecture that depends on window addressable memory (WAM) concepts to achieve both high performance and a compact solution. The implementation of these WAM concepts in a full custom application specific integrated circuit (ASIC) is the key to achieving these objectives. The ASICs were developed as part of the Racal and MOD jointly funded VHPIC Application Demonstrator (VAD) project. This forms part of the VAD programme which is led from RSRE.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Signal processing requirements for future ESM systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Signal Processing for ESM Systems
abstract: Reviews the requirements for signal processing in modern military ESM systems. It must be emphasised that this paper refers entirely to information published in the open literature and is based on the personal opinions of the author, which are non-attributable to The Ministry of Defence.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Signal Processing for ESM Systems
abstract: The Admiralty Research Establishment (ARE) is supporting research on ESM digital signal processing techniques to provide the functions of automatic detection, surveillance and identification of radar emitters for application in future naval ESM systems. Naval ESM systems are required to operate at high data rates (1 Mbps) and with a low processing latency. A high level of correct reporting and correct emitter identification is required in high pulse density environments including complex emitters which may have significant overlap in bearing and frequency. This paper describes the ARE research programme, which has two key aims. Firstly, to develop new techniques capable of providing a high probability of detection and unambiguous identification of complex radar emitters in dense scenarios. Secondly, to demonstrate the performance of selected techniques in real time using parallel processing methods and VLSI signal processing devices.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A parallel processing solution to ESM
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Signal Processing for ESM Systems
abstract: The Admiralty Research Establishment (ARE) is responsible for developing ESM signal processing algorithms capable of detecting and identifying radar emitters in complex, high density naval scenarios. An important processing stage in the algorithms is to assemble individual pulses from each emitter into pulse chains. This process is termed deinterleaving. The performance of the deinterleaver in processing complex radar waveforms in a high pulse density environment is fundamental to the reliable operation of the entire ESM system. ARE has developed a sophisticated deinterleaver (termed DIF6) which operates in two stages. Firstly, pulses are merged into clusters formed from the basic pulse measurements. Secondly, the time differences between pulses in each cluster are used to form a time of arrival difference (ToAD) histogram. Signals which may be overlapped in pulse repetition interval are detected by locating peaks in the ToAD histogram and gated from the input data. Several iterations of this process may be required to detect all pulse chains. The deinterleaver then forms a characterised pulse chain which is output to other processing stages in the ESM signal processor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New processing techniques for ESM using partial coherence
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Signal Processing for ESM Systems
abstract: The trend in naval scenarios towards greater complexity in radar signals and high duty cycle transmissions both from own ship and from the signal environment of interest puts even greater demands on the receiver and signal processing of ESM systems. In particular, a growing need exists for large dynamic range, wide bandwidth and high frequency-resolution systems that have the ability to automatically identify a wide range of threats. Optical arrangements based upon acousto-optical (AO) Bragg cells are being investigated by many researchers because they offer the promise of high-speed processing, particularly in the form of spectrum analysers used for channelised receivers. This paper describes recent research at ARE on novel system designs using optical partial-coherence processing which shows that the currently observed limits are not fundamental and that optical arrangements do indeed offer potential not only as channelised receivers, but as powerful signal processing systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
